title: A closed semiabelian subgroup with trivial invertible-prime torsion is finite
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G/k$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $\ell$ be a prime integer whose image in $k$ is nonzero. Write $[\ell]_H:H\to H$ for addition of $\ell$ copies of a point, and let $e_H:\operatorname{Spec}k\to H$ be the identity section. Define $H[\ell]=H\times_{H,[\ell]_H,e_H}\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If its identity section $\operatorname{Spec}k\to H[\ell]$ is an isomorphism, then $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Neither reducedness nor connectedness of $H$ is assumed. Rank zero tori and zero-dimensional abelian quotients are allowed.

source.place: Brian Conrad, Semistable reduction for abelian varieties, Corollary 3.3, printed p.8, restricted to algebraically closed k and an invertible prime. Local copy WANTED; read the author PDF online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/DarmonCM/2011Notes/SemistableReduction.pdf . This is the closed-subgroup input of the proof of Theorem 4.4, printed p.13.

proof.text: A finite affine cover of $G$ by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras restricts under the closed immersion $H\hookrightarrow G$ to spectra of quotient algebras. These quotients are still finitely generated, so $H$ is of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $H$: the identity component $H^0$ is a clopen subgroup and $B=(H^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected finite-type group with $|B|=|H^0|$. Its inclusion in $G$ is a closed subgroup: reduction is a closed immersion, and the inclusions compose by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products].

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, reduction to the smooth connected reduced identity component; Stacks Tags 0B7R, 047R, 047P and 047N as in the cited existing component node

proof.text: Write $j:B\hookrightarrow H$. On every $k$-algebra $R$, if $b\in B(R)$ satisfies $[\ell]b=0$, then $j(b)\in H[\ell](R)$, so $j(b)=0$ by the assumed isomorphism $H[\ell]\simeq\operatorname{Spec}k$. Injectivity of $j(R)$ gives $b=0$. Thus the identity identifies $B[\ell]$ with the trivial group functor, hence with $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, torsion vanishing inherited by the reduced identity subgroup

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-semiabelian-subgroup] to $B\hookrightarrow G$, using smoothness and connectedness from step 1. Obtain an exact sequence $1\to T\to B\xrightarrow{q}A\to1$ of fppf sheaves, where $T=(\mathbf G_m)^r$ and $A$ is an abelian variety.

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, semiabelianity of the reduced identity subgroup via Corollary 3.2

proof.text: If $r>0$, the nonconstant polynomial $P(X)=1+X+\cdots+X^{\ell-1}$ has a root $\zeta\in k$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Since $P(1)=\ell\ne0$ and $P(0)=1$, one has $\zeta\ne1,0$; the identity $(X-1)P(X)=X^\ell-1$ gives $\zeta^\ell=1$. The point $(\zeta,1,\ldots,1)\in T(k)$ is nonidentity and killed by $\ell$. The subgroup injection $T(k)\to B(k)$ contradicts step 2. Therefore $r=0$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, vanishing of the toric rank; elementary geometric-series calculation replaces the full torus torsion-order formula

proof.text: Now $T=1$. Exactness in step 3 makes $q$ injective on sections and locally surjective. Every local lift of a section of $A$ agrees with every other lift on overlaps because their difference belongs to $T=1$; the sheaf gluing axiom gives a unique global lift. Thus $q$ is an isomorphism of represented fppf sheaves, and hence of group schemes (evaluate the inverse natural transformation on the identity of each representing scheme). Consequently $B$ is an abelian variety. By [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat], its finite kernel $B[\ell]$ has order $\ell^{2g}$ for $g=\dim B$. Step 2 gives order one; since $\ell\geq2$, this forces $g=0$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, the abelian-variety case; Stacks Tag 03RP (proposition-review-abelian-varieties) and Tag 0BFG (lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d) for the existing torsion-order node

proof.text: The homeomorphism $|B|=|H^0|$ from step 1 gives $\dim H^0=0$. By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $H$ has finitely many clopen components and each is isomorphic to $H^0$. Any chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets lies in one component: an irreducible subset cannot meet a clopen set and its complement. Thus $\dim H=0$. Apply [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] to $H\hookrightarrow G$, a closed subscheme of a finite-type $k$-scheme with topological dimension zero. Its structure morphism is finite, without requiring $H$ reduced or connected.

source.place: Corollary 3.3 proof, justification of the initial reduction and final finiteness; Stacks Tag 06LH (varieties-lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0)

proof_origin.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3, printed p.8; author PDF read online, local archive WANTED. Expanded the component reduction and replaced the torus order count by a geometric-series root.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q133-9849841d0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item statement is unchanged; I tested it on trivial H, constant prime-to-ℓ H, nonreduced μ_p⊂G_m, G_m and an abelian variety, and it holds in each. Step 1: H is of finite type; lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component gives H^0 clopen and B=(H^0)_red smooth and connected with |B|=|H^0|; the reduction is a closed immersion and the composition comes from lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products. That H^0→H is a closed immersion (clopen) is elementary but not written out. Step 2 is an elementary R-point argument through the subgroup injections, so the nonreduced case is covered. Step 3 applies the new node to B. Step 4 takes a root ζ≠1 of 1+X+…+X^{ℓ-1} (P(1)=ℓ≠0); the point (ζ,1,…,1) contradicts step 2, so r=0. Step 5: with trivial kernel, unique local lifts glue, so q is an isomorphism; lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat gives ℓ^{2g}=1, so g=0. Step 6: lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates (finitely many clopen components, each isomorphic to H^0) gives dim H=0, and lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite gives finiteness without reducedness or properness. New node lem-sfb-smooth-connected-semiabelian-subgroup is Conrad Cor. 3.2 over algebraically closed k; it is true, self-contained, statement-only and not a restatement of the item (no torsion hypothesis, no finiteness conclusion). The DAG search over semiabelian/subgroup found no duplicate (geometric-semiabelian-split-quotient, normal-semiabelian-generic-torus-quotient and the subtorus-quotient nodes all assume the semiabelian structure). Conrad is not in the local literature (inherited WANTED); I checked it from knowledge of Cor. 3.2/3.3. Batch-5 flag: lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat (Stacks 0BFG) reaches lem-trf-rational-sequence-polynomial-forward-difference, which is only Newton-series integration of polynomial-difference sequences (Stacks 00JZ). It is a general algebra lemma that neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives, not a step of their proofs, so the citation is accepted. tool_uses accepted as generic. No changes.
